summary: Tested 'show more' recipes functionality on both ChatPage and DiabetesMealsPage. All 7 backend API tests passed (100%). The 'show more' functionality correctly extracts context from [Context: ...] format, generates NEW different recipes (not cached), and returns structured_recipes in the API response for both endpoints.
passed_tests: Main Chat: Initial recipe generation works correctly (POST /api/chat/send)
Main Chat: 'show more' with [Context: ...] format returns structured_recipes (4 Italian vegetarian recipes)
Main Chat: Various 'show more' phrases detected ('more recipes', 'different recipes', 'give me more')
Main Chat: 'show more' returns DIFFERENT recipes than initial response (skip_cache=true works)
Diabetes Chat: 'show more' request returns structured_recipes (3 diabetes-friendly recipes)
Diabetes Chat: Various 'show more' phrases work ('more options', 'different recipes', 'alternatives')
Context Extraction: [Context: Mood=X, MealType=Y, Dietary=Z, Cuisines=W] format properly parsed
critical_code_review_comments: Backend implementation is correct: extract_context_params() in chat.py properly parses [Context:] format
Main chat (lines 879-885): is_show_more is detected first, then extract_context_params extracts parameters
Diabetes chat (lines 456-464): is_show_more patterns properly detected and new recipes generated
structured_recipes is returned in both endpoints' responses for 'show more' requests

success_rate.frontend: Not fully tested due to UI automation session persistence issue

seed_data_creation: None - tests create temporary users and use AI-generated recipes
context_for_next_testing_agent: The 'show more' functionality works correctly at the API level. Key points: (1) Frontend sends '[Context: Mood=X, MealType=Y, Dietary=Z, Cuisines=W]\n\nshow more' format, (2) Backend's extract_context_params() parses this context, (3) Recipe generation is triggered with skip_cache=true to get different recipes, (4) Both /api/chat/send and /api/diabetes/chat return structured_recipes array in response. UI automation tests had trouble with session persistence after registration, but this is unrelated to the 'show more' feature.
